chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The husband who makes a vow of abstention from his wife is given a four-month waiting period; if he wills, he retains her 'with good conduct' or releases her 'with kindness.' If he decides on divorce, it is a single revocable divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِرَجْعَتِهَا: Has the right to take her back (revocation)
key_terms.اَلْمُؤْلِي: The husband who makes a vow of abstention from his wife
key_terms.بِمَعْرُوفٍ: With good conduct / in a fair manner
key_terms.يُوقَفُ: Is given a waiting period / is suspended

ai.seo_question: What is the legal procedure and waiting period for a husband who vows abstention (Ila') from his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural outcome of 'Ila'' (vow of abstention), specifying that if the husband does not resume relations within the four-month period, the resulting divorce is classified as a single, revocable divorce (Talaqah Wahidah). This ruling grants the husband exclusive authority to revoke the divorce and resume marital relations during the 'Iddah period without requiring a new marriage contract, a nuance emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to distinguish it from irrevocable divorces.
